h: Remembering and Guarding the Holiness of Shabbos

p: and there are several differences in it
in the first Dibros it is written,
"and He rested on the seventh day;
And in the second it is written (Devarim 5:15):
"And you shall remember that you were a slave
in the land of Mitzrayim," etc.,
in the question of the wise son (Devarim 6:20):
"What are the testimonies, the statutes and the laws
"then you shall say to your son:
"and Hashem commanded us to do," etc.
to the reason for the statutes?
which Hashem commanded us to do
But the essence of his question is:
since the purpose and intent of the mitzvos
"And Hashem commanded us to do," etc.,
and likewise it is written above,
"and I will let them hear My words,
to fear Me all the days";
the statutes and the laws," etc.,
לְמַעַן תִּירָא אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְגוֹ׳
"so that you will fear Hashem your God," etc.
for the essential purpose of the mitzvos,
and as is written in the holy Zohar
with the will of the heart
toward the Holy One, blessed is He,
He does not ask of us
And about this the son asks:
"What are the testimonies, the statutes and the laws
why did He give us so many mitzvos?
He should have commanded only the purpose:
to love and to fear Hashem.
that in truth, were it not for the yetzer hara,
through which Torah learning was implanted in their hearts
(as is written in the Midrash; Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2).
like a fetus in its mother's womb,
to take us out with a strong hand;
which were a smiting for Mitzrayim
of the ten kelipos of impurity,
and brought them into one attribute
And this is "and He took us out from there," etc.;
for this requires six hundred thirteen mitzvos,
which are six hundred thirteen kinds of counsels,
because there is the yetzer hara,

p: at the time of the giving of the Torah:
in the first Dibros it is written (Shemos 20:8):
for on the part of Yisrael
only an arousal from below is needed,
to remember Shabbos with the mouth,
comes of itself from Hashem Yisbarach;
"to know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you";
the Shabbos day and sanctified it"
for Hashem Yisbarach placed in it
"and He rested on the seventh day," etc.
And this is like what is said in the She'iltos
just as I rested on it."
הֵם דְּרָכָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
are the ways of the Holy One, blessed is He;
for the Holy One, blessed is He, too
as is written in the Midrash
"The Holy One, blessed is He, is not so;
to fulfill "and you shall walk in His ways" (Devarim 28:9).
just as I rested on it."
for through remembering with the mouth alone
they will merit the holiness of Shabbos
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach;
for this is what the term "remember" indicates:
a place where there is no forgetting.
This is not so in the second Dibros,
for now guarding is already needed,
so that he not forget Shabbos
they will bring holiness into Shabbos.
"And you shall remember that you were a slave," etc.
to remember that we were so sunk
"and Hashem your God took you out from there
with a strong hand and an outstretched arm."
For this extra guarding is needed,
for through guarding the whole day
they themselves will bring holiness into Shabbos.
And so we find in Parashas Ki Sisa,
in the command of the work of the Mishkan,
that this was said after the corruption,
"And He gave to Moshe when He finished."
the Ramban, of blessed memory, wrote
that everything was said in order
and they were commanded about the work of the Mishkan
before the episode of the Calf
of the command of the work of the Mishkan
that they were going to corrupt,
for were it not for the corruption,
the Shechinah would have been fit to be
in every place where Yisrael dwelt,
as before the corruption of Adam HaRishon,
and the whole camp of Yisrael would have been
like the holiness of the place of the Mishkan.
And here, since it was said
according to how it would be after the corruption,
therefore it says there in the passage of Shabbos:
"But My Shabbosos you shall guard," etc.;
"and you shall guard the Shabbos," etc.;
וְשָׁמְרוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְגוֹ׳ (שְׁמוֹת לא, יג–טז)
"and Bnei Yisrael shall guard the Shabbos," etc. (Shemos 31:13–16)
for since the yetzer hara would return,
guarding is needed so as not to forget;
the whole Shabbos day, on their part,
they will merit to bring holiness into Shabbos;

inlineHeadings.text: Remembering Before Sin and Guarding Afterward

p: And this is the matter of
what is written in the Midrash
corresponding to the seven days of Creation, etc.;
on Shabbos, what can you say?
מְחַלְלֶיהָ מוֹת יוּמָת (שְׁמוֹת לא, יד) וְכוּלֵּי
'Those who desecrate it shall surely die' (Shemos 31:14)," etc.
that it is written of it, "those who desecrate it," etc.
that the yetzer hara will enter
and the holiness will be forgotten by him
he said of this: "All is vanity."
at the time of the giving of the Torah,
which is a place where there is no forgetting,
and forgetting does not exist there,
so that it should be fixed in the heart
And nevertheless it is written afterward
כִּי שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים עָשָׂה ה׳ וְגוֹ׳
"for in six days Hashem made," etc.;
by which they will merit to make the Shabbos,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה יִזְכּוּ אַחַר כָּךְ
through this they will afterward merit
the holiness that is fixed and established
And this is what we say in the Kiddush of the day:
a remembrance of the work of Creation";
where the reason for Shabbos is stated,
where it says "it is a sign forever,
"a good gift, whose name is Shabbos,"
which is a holiness fixed and established
"to know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you."
that Yisrael bring holiness into Shabbos,
"a remembrance of the Exodus from Mitzrayim"
And the matter of remembering the Exodus from Mitzrayim,
about which they were warned several times,
that a person not fall in his own eyes
and knows the afflictions of his heart,
and that he not despair, chas v'shalom.
the remembrance of the Exodus from Mitzrayim:
that although they were sunk there
like a fetus in its mother's womb,
Hashem took us out from there;
and so Hashem Yisbarach will help
everyone who wishes to return in truth.
like the point of a needle,
and I will open for you openings
And they say in the name of
הַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה
the Baal Shem Tov, may the memory of the tzaddik be for a blessing:
must pass through from one side to the other,
to the depths of the heart."
that is mentioned in the utterance (Shemos 20:2):
Who took you out of the land of Mitzrayim."
And the Ramban, of blessed memory, wrote
that the Exodus from Mitzrayim includes
the creation of the world and Providence;
And according to what was said above, it is
"Anochi — in it is the kaf of Keser," etc.,
that Yisrael are bound to the root
therefore the Exodus from Mitzrayim is mentioned,
that even one who is sunk, chas v'shalom,
לֹא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח (שְׁמוּאֵל ב יד, יד)
"none of them will be cast away" (Shmuel II 14:14),
since they are bound at the root
to return to Hashem and to cleave to Him,
as in the days of our going out of the land of Mitzrayim.
